sec: RPGN biopsy: light microscopy & IF patterns · p779

items.q: The light-microscopy hallmark of crescentic glomerulonephritis described here is:
opts: Proliferation of parietal epithelial cells with fibrin, the number of crescents mattering
Segmental sclerosis with hyalinosis at the vascular pole
Basement membrane thinning with splitting of the lamina densa
items.exp: LM shows crescentic GN due to proliferation of parietal epithelial cells with fibrin; the number of crescents is an important factor. (Book p779)

items.q: Fill up: The crescents of crescentic glomerulonephritis are formed by proliferation of ______ epithelial cells with fibrin.
items.exp: Crescents arise from proliferation of parietal epithelial cells together with fibrin; their number matters prognostically. (Book p779)

items.q: Match each immunofluorescence pattern in the biopsy figure with its image label — 1) No deposits  2) Uniform bright linear staining along the capillary walls  3) Coarse granular staining of capillary loops and mesangium … A) Linear IF  B) Negative IF  C) Diffuse granular IF
items.exp: The figure panels are labelled: A. negative IF; B. diffuse granular IF; C. linear IF (with D. granular IF) — the linear pattern being the one written in text for type I RPGN. (Book p779)

items.q: Linear immunofluorescence in type I RPGN occurs because the antibodies are directed against a structural antigen of the glomerular basement membrane.
opts: True — linear IF is the imprint of anti-GBM antibody binding
False — linear IF is typical of immune-complex disease
False — linear IF in RPGN is due to cellular crescents alone
True, but linear IF is seen only in type III disease
items.exp: Type I RPGN (Goodpasture syndrome) shows linear IgG ± C3 along the glomerular capillary wall, being anti-GBM antibody disease; the granular patterns of panels B/D arise from immune-complex deposition. (Book p779)

items.q: Match each IF pattern with its listed important association — 1) Linear IF  2) Granular IF … A) Immune-complex deposition, e.g. diabetes mellitus and light chain disease  B) Goodpasture disease
items.exp: Important IF associations: linear IF → Goodpasture disease; granular IF → diabetes mellitus and light chain disease. (Book p779)

items.q: Which condition is NOT listed among the important associations of the immunofluorescence patterns?
opts: Goodpasture disease, associated with linear IF
Diabetes mellitus, associated with granular IF
Light chain disease, associated with granular IF
items.exp: The associations printed are Goodpasture disease (linear), diabetes mellitus and light chain disease (granular); PSGN is not on that list. (Book p779)

items.q: A diabetic patient with nephrotic-range proteinuria and renal failure has a renal biopsy showing coarse granular immunofluorescence; the listed important association is:
items.exp: Granular IF is importantly associated with diabetes mellitus and light chain disease; Goodpasture disease goes with linear IF. (Book p779)
